result.title: Beyond Retrieval: Evidence Access and Event Aggregation in Agent Memory
result.summary: Questions about an agent's history often require aggregating events, which retrieval alone does not resolve. We combine source-preserving evidence access with executable aggregation. Trajectory Memory (TM) retains the original trajectory and constructs a source-addressable reading view at question time. TallyMem augments it with a reusable event ledger, model-generated event specifications and deterministic execution. With a commit-specific adaptation on 776 questions from 99 held-out MINTEval repositories, TallyMem raises Qwen3-32B exact match from 35.2% to 49.0%, a 13.8-point gain over TM; gains span 12.8-13.9 points across three readers. A controlled probe with event sets parsed independently from raw logs shows an 11.0-point gain, from 82.8% to 93.8%, without routing. On full AMA-Bench, the routed system yields a smaller 1.3-point gain, from 69.8% to 71.1%. These results support executable aggregation on tasks that require combining events, with benefits dependent on the task and event specification, the largest residual system-error category in our diagnostic analysis.

AI.brief_summary: 针对需聚合事件的智能体历史问答，论文把「保留原始轨迹、按问题构建来源可寻址阅读视图」的 Trajectory Memory 与「模型生成事件规格 + 确定性执行的事件账本」TallyMem 结合，在 MINTEval 与 AMA-Bench 上报告增益。
AI.relevance_reason: 其中「保留源证据并按需访问 + 可执行聚合」的线索或可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选与跨事件信息聚合的对应问题，收益依任务与事件规格而变的诊断也可能类比 latent 推理的贡献分配，迁移性需人工判断。
